title: Global bond sell-off sends 30-year UST yield to a 19-year high
content:
A global bond sell-off intensified this week as the 30-year US Treasury yield surged to **5.33%**, its highest level in 19 years, while Japan's 10-year JGB yield also climbed to a three-decade high. The move came as gross US federal debt topped **$40 trillion** for the first time, with the fiscal year-to-date deficit already near $1.8 trillion, deepening investor unease over Washington's borrowing trajectory.

Sticky inflation, elevated oil prices and uncertainty over new Fed chair Kevin Warsh's policy approach added to the pressure, pushing the 10-year yield toward **4.75%**. Equities wobbled as higher long-end yields squeezed valuations, underlining how fiscal strain has become a cross-asset story reaching well beyond the Treasury market.

title: Brent gives back gains as US readies 'economic warfare' on Iran
content:
Brent crude fell **1.4%** to around **$93/bbl** on Monday, giving back part of a two-week rally, as traders awaited details of a sweeping US sanctions package against Iran. President Trump has vowed an 'economic warfare' campaign alongside a continued blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent promised an 'economic D-Day' for Tehran, with shipping through the strait still far below normal.

WTI slipped to around $85.70/bbl, with Monday's fall reflecting profit-taking after Brent's advance toward **$95/bbl** last week rather than any easing of risk. Analysts said the standoff still threatens a supply shock that could reignite the inflation pressures already unsettling bond markets.

title: Wall Street posts weekly loss as bond volatility bites; bitcoin soars
content:
US equities booked a second straight weekly loss, with the S&P 500 down **1.4%**, the Nasdaq off **2.5%** and the Dow shedding 1.8% over the week, as surging Treasury yields undercut risk appetite. Stocks staged a partial recovery on Friday, with the Dow rallying around 1% and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each adding roughly 0.4%.

Bitcoin bucked the trend, surging to around **$77,000** for its best week in two years, as some investors rotated into crypto amid the bond market turmoil. The divergence points to fragile sentiment: rate-sensitive equities remain vulnerable to further yield spikes even as pockets of risk appetite persist.
